newsitem.title: USA: MTel says cash flow positive in Q4.
newsitem.headline: MTel says cash flow positive in Q4.

text.p: Paging company Mobile Telecommunications Technologies Corp (MTel) on Thursday said preliminary operating results showed positive consolidated operating cash flow of $3.2 million for fourth quarter 1996.

This compares with a negative cash flow of $24 million a year ago, which included an $18.3 million one time item for the launch of a narrowband Personal Communications Services network. Full results will be released on February 27.
MTel said there was no truth to rumors about the company having liquidity problems. It said it has $14 million cash on hand and over $30 million bank credit.

"Our stock has been pressured this week by speculation about the company's liquidity and other issues," said MTel chief financial officer Robert Kaiser. "This speculation has no basis in fact," he added.

MTel said that preliminary data showed fourth quarter 1996 revenues at $89.6 million, 21 percent above the $74.1 million of a year ago. Operating cash flow for SkyTel one-way paging was $26.0 million against $19.1 million a year ago.
Total pagers in service rose by over 51,000 in the quarter on a consolidated basis, with net adds in one-way paging of 35,000 in the quarter.
MTel said reconciliation of prior periods is complete and will reduce year-end pagers in service by around 9,000.

"While we are certainly pleased with the preliminary financial results for the fourth quarter, I am even more excited about the momentum which is building towards the April 1997 introduction of our advanced messaging products," said chief executive John Stupka.
MTel shares were 7/16 lower at 6-1/4 at 1030 EST/1530 GMT, having fallen from more than $8 at the end of last week. (( Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
